definition: The EuroMatrix is a project that ran from September 2006 to February 2009.
details: The project aimed to develop and improve machine translation (MT) systems between all official languages of the European Union (EU). EuroMatrix was followed up by another project EuroMatrixPlus (March 2009 to February 2012).

explainer.lead: EuroMatrix was a machine-translation project that ran from September 2006 to February 2009. Its goal was broad: develop and improve translation systems between all official languages of the European Union, with follow-up work continuing in EuroMatrixPlus.

tiers.eli5: Imagine trying to make better computer translators for every official language used across a large group of countries. EuroMatrix was a project working toward that goal for the European Union. It finished in February 2009, and a follow-up project called EuroMatrixPlus carried the work forward.
tiers.practitioner: Treat EuroMatrix as a multilingual machine-translation project, not as an installable translation library. Its scope was the development and improvement of MT systems between all official EU languages. When tracing later work, distinguish the original project, which ended in February 2009, from EuroMatrixPlus, which ran from March 2009 to February 2012.
tiers.paperLevel: EuroMatrix was an MT system-development project active from September 2006 to February 2009. Given the set L of all official European Union languages, its objective was to develop and improve machine translation between those languages rather than address only one language pair. Its successor was EuroMatrixPlus, active from March 2009 to February 2012.

explainer.example: Suppose a public notice written in one official EU language must be read in another. Within EuroMatrix's goal, a machine-translation system would take the notice as input and produce its translation in the requested official language, with the project seeking better systems for such language pairs.

usedIn.name: Machine translation research
usedIn.detail: The project focused on developing and improving MT systems.

usedIn.name: Multilingual EU communication
usedIn.detail: Its target setting was translation between all official languages of the European Union.

explainer.intuition: Instead of improving translation for just one pair of languages, EuroMatrix aimed across the European Union's complete set of official languages. The central idea was to make machine translation better across that multilingual landscape.
howItWorks: Take all official European Union languages as the project's language scope.
Develop and improve machine-translation systems for those languages.
Aim to support translation between the languages, not merely one selected pair.
Run the original effort from September 2006 through February 2009.
Continue the work through EuroMatrixPlus from March 2009 to February 2012.
explainer.whyItMatters: EuroMatrix addressed machine translation across the European Union's official languages rather than treating multilingual translation as a single-language-pair problem. EuroMatrixPlus provided a direct continuation of that effort.
misconceptions: EuroMatrix was a project, not a single translation algorithm.
The original project ended in February 2009.
EuroMatrixPlus was a separate follow-up project, not another name for the same dates.

diagram.caption: EuroMatrix targeted translation among the EU's official languages and was followed by EuroMatrixPlus.
